title: Quarterly surge cadence and fallback playbook for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an operational playbook and roadmap slice for predictable surge handling and fallback behavior for Dedicated capacity in Q2. This ticket aggregates acceptance criteria, cross-functional milestones, rollout steps, and required telemetry so Platform, Runtime, and SRE teams can run a coordinated pilot and then hand off to oncall and account teams. The intent is to reduce customer-observed latency degradation during surge windows and ensure automatic, safe fallbacks between tiers (hosted -> dedicated -> compatible model variants) while preserving revenue commitments.
OKRs: O: Improve Dedicated capacity reliability and cost predictability during burst events (Q2)
KR1: Reduce 95th-percentile tail latency impact during simulated 2x-4x surge by >=40% compared to baseline
KR2: Validate safe fallback policy that avoids customer-facing errors for 99.9% of synthetic surge traffic
KR3: Document and enable runbook for sales/CS for 3 priority customers in pilot with clear escalation paths
milestones: M1: Runbook draft and review with Runtime/Infra/SRE (2026-02-15)
M2: Canary simulation harness and surge test matrix ready (2026-03-05)
M3: Pilot with dedicated pool + prewarm + fallback enabled for 3 customers (2026-04-01)
M4: Post-pilot retro and acceptance gate for org-wide rollout (2026-04-20)
acceptance_criteria: Playbook contains decision tree for surge detection thresholds, priority routing, and rollback criteria
Runbook includes run-as-role steps for Platform oncall and Sales ops to enact reserved increases and apply fallbacks
Telemetry dashboards exposing per-pool latency P50/P95/P99, prewarm utilization, and fallback frequency are published
Automated simulation reproduces surge scenarios with deterministic results and documented test cases
stakeholders: Mateo Alvarez (Runtime Eng) - kernel and batching constraints
Janelle Kim (Sales Ops) - pilot customer coordination
Design Ops (consult) - dashboard layout and alert UX
risks: Over-aggressive prewarm increases could materially raise monthly committed cost if not gated
Fallbacks to smaller model variants may cause quality regressions for sensitive customers
Cross-region coordination required for some customers adds orchestration complexity and latency variance
rollout_plan: 1) Finalize playbook and acceptance criteria with Runtime & SRE
2) Implement surge detection signals and telemetry in staging; wire dashboards
3) Run three controlled surge simulations (2x, 3x, 4x) and capture results
4) Enable pilot mode for 3 pre-consented customers with enhanced observability and a rollback window
5) Execute retro, adjust configuration (prewarm thresholds, fallback latency SLOs), and publish org rollout guidance
